review_method: Root complete written-module source review, accepted full native statement/generality reports, and explicit comparison of exact operator algebra, substitution, determinant constructions and coefficient estimates. Both concrete facts/mechanisms are recorded per pair, with key shared-parent/specialization cases expanded. Completed-only synthesis.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Multivariate Hasse laws act on one polynomial with a chosen multi-index. The Wronskian module forms a square matrix of consecutive univariate Hasse derivatives of a whole family, then studies determinant coefficients and independence. Singleton transport provides an operator bridge, but matrix nonvanishing needs characteristic-zero Vandermonde/cancellation arguments beyond exact derivative formulas.
blocks.default_action: Share the characteristic-safe Hasse operator identities and singleton compatibility; retain determinant and family independence arguments as separate layers.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: The operator API gives individual divided derivatives and composition. Generalized Wronskians select finite families of such operators, while Kronecker substitution preserves bounded-degree information and its derivative span uses polynomial scalar coefficients. Closure under differentiating a span needs the derivative product rule on those scalar coefficients; generator derivative formulas alone are insufficient. A nonvanishing determinant is not implied by one derivative identity.
blocks.default_action: Use the shared derivative formulas as explicit inputs; preserve finite-support substitution, span and row-selection results independently.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Separation uses the Hasse API to split derivatives across independent variable blocks, but also performs coefficient extraction, basis decomposition and integer factor descent. Disjoint-support composition and independence-of-variables justify the split; they do not supply the separated representation or arithmetic primitivity. Exact natural binomial scalars must be retained in general characteristic.
blocks.default_action: Share factorwise/disjoint Hasse primitives; retain separated coefficient geometry and arithmetic descent as independent proof content.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Translation packages Hasse evaluations as polynomial coefficients and is invertible over rings. A Wronskian packages different derivatives of different family members into a determinant. Translation coefficient identities can explain divided normalization, but they do not prove determinant nonvanishing or distinct-degree Vandermonde formulas. Real/commutative ring translation injectivity has no characteristic-zero independence-detection conclusion by itself.
blocks.default_action: Coordinate the Hasse coefficient interpretation without merging invertible translation with a family determinant criterion.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Taylor and Kronecker are both universal substitutions, but Taylor shifts generators independently and has a ring inverse; Kronecker collapses many variables to powers of one and is only injective on bounded-degree subspaces. Its Hasse-span argument studies derivatives of the substituted polynomial and needs chain-rule coefficients, unlike translation's simple additive composition.
blocks.default_action: Share aeval/monomial/substitution laws; preserve bounded injectivity and chain-rule operator spans separately from global translation inversion.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Translation expands around an arbitrary point, preserving the same multivariate polynomial space. Distinguished-variable extraction views a polynomial as univariate with polynomial coefficients, then forms a basis of their span and separates variables. These are different coordinate decompositions; Taylor coefficient/Hasse evaluation is not the coefficient-span basis or primitive factorization theorem.
blocks.default_action: Use existing coefficient extraction/substitution homomorphism laws in both settings, keeping translation and separated tensor-style decomposition APIs distinct.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Coefficient estimates bound norms or degrees of arbitrary Hasse determinant entries and permutation products. Wronskian nonvanishing computes a specific coefficient and proves it is nonzero, using distinct degrees and characteristic-zero factorial/Vandermonde factors. An upper magnitude bound does not supply a nonzero lower bound, and nonvanishing gives no uniform coefficient height by itself.
blocks.default_action: Share determinant expansion and finite-product infrastructure; retain quantitative upper bounds and algebraic nonvanishing as different statements.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Coefficient-height bounds control every entry or determinant for prescribed derivative orders. Generalized Wronskian existence selects orders making a determinant nonzero. Bounds on all candidates do not construct a nonzero one, while existence does not bound its magnitude without the separate degree/height assumptions.
blocks.default_action: Keep selection/nonvanishing separate from uniform magnitude and degree estimates; their later joint use is dependency, not duplication.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Coefficient estimates and degree inequalities control a polynomial/determinant numerically. Separated-factor construction provides an equality, independent factor families and integral factors; its degree bounds use exact degree additivity for nonzero separated factors. A determinant upper bound neither proves integrality nor preserves degrees through arbitrary cancellations.
blocks.default_action: Share the determinant degree bound where used; retain exact separated product and primitive/GCD descent data separately from norm upper bounds.

special_pairs.comparison: Singleton-variable Hasse transport identifies each matrix entry under the canonical polynomial equivalence; applying the algebra map to the determinant gives the corresponding determinant bridge. It does not equate the raw current multivariate and univariate representations definitionally.
special_pairs.action: Use singleton compatibility for coherent Hasse Wronskian normalization; keep the determinant construction API decision separate.

special_pairs.comparison: Factorial scaling relates iterated ordinary derivatives to divided derivatives without division. The binomial determinant formula over a characteristic-zero field divides row factorials in the Vandermonde evaluation computation. The latter field/CharZero premises cannot be erased from its quotient formula just because the scaled identity is more general.
special_pairs.action: Separate characteristic-safe scaled identities from factorial-inverse determinant normalizations.

special_pairs.comparison: The partial derivative raises one Hasse order with a successor scalar. Differentiating after Kronecker also differentiates each substitution polynomial, sums over variables by the chain rule, and transports coefficients. The successor identity supplies only one component.
special_pairs.action: Reuse the operator successor law inside the genuine substitution chain rule.

special_pairs.comparison: Disjoint derivative orders compose without a binomial factor. Separated product differentiation additionally proves that each factor is independent of the other block's variables and applies the single-variable Hasse transport.
special_pairs.action: Share disjoint composition and variable-independence extraction; retain the full factorwise separated formula.

special_pairs.comparison: The generic independent-factor rule pulls out a factor with degree0 on every differentiated coordinate. The separated product law applies it twice, once to each variable block, then identifies the univariate derivative.
special_pairs.action: Keep one general independence rule and derive the separated block law using the verified coordinate bridge.

special_pairs.comparison: The first computes a Hasse derivative of a single-variable embedded polynomial. The second combines that special computation with a separate polynomial in disjoint ordinary variables.
special_pairs.action: Retain the embedding compatibility as reusable input to the full separated-product result.

special_pairs.comparison: Ring translation has an explicit global inverse, so it preserves nonzero polynomials unconditionally. Kronecker identifies bounded exponent tuples through a base representation and fails global injectivity when different monomials share an encoded exponent.
special_pairs.action: Do not unify these as an unconditional substitution-injectivity theorem; retain the verified degree-box restriction on Kronecker.

special_pairs.comparison: Taylor coefficient d is a Hasse derivative evaluated at the translation vector. Nested coeffNone extraction is the coefficient at a split exponent after the option-variable polynomial equivalence; it uses no center and does not evaluate derivatives.
special_pairs.action: Keep shifted coefficient evaluation separate from exact variable-block coefficient transport.

special_pairs.comparison: Taylor reconstruction is a finite expansion in powers of X-alpha with evaluated derivative coefficients. Distinguished-variable expansion is an exact polynomial identity with coefficients still polynomials in the remaining variables. The latter is not obtained by evaluating all remaining variables without losing information.
special_pairs.action: Share finite polynomial expansion mechanisms; retain the coefficient-object and translation differences.

special_pairs.comparison: Both start from determinant multilinearity or a Leibniz expansion. One takes absolute-value upper bounds, sums over l! permutations and yields l! C^l. The other preserves an exact weighted sum over independent row choices, including cancellations.
special_pairs.action: Reuse determinant/multilinear APIs, retaining exact expansion and norm majorization as distinct outputs.

special_pairs.comparison: The uniform determinant degree bound holds for all chosen row orders, including a zero determinant. Integral separated-factor existence first chooses a nonzero determinant, descends its factors, and uses nonzero separated degree identities to transfer that upper bound to each factor.
special_pairs.action: Keep the generic degree inequality as one prerequisite of the stronger existence-and-factorization theorem.

special_pairs.comparison: The coefficient-height theorem bounds an arbitrary prescribed Hasse determinant. The separated identity equates a structured determinant with a product of two Wronskians. Product equality alone does not bound each factor's coefficients without additional integral nonzero-factor arguments.
special_pairs.action: Retain the independent determinant upper estimate and exact factorization; handle factor-height extraction as its own verified layer.
